name: atomicadd
algorithm: t workers (Mk: tasks; Go: goroutines; C, Rust and Zig: OS threads) each add 1 to one shared atomic 64-bit counter n times: Mk atomic.AtomicInt.Add (lock xadd, then the overflow check), Rust AtomicI64::fetch_add, Go atomic.Int64.Add, Zig std.atomic.Value(i64).fetchAdd, C11 atomic_fetch_add, every one sequentially consistent. Prints the counter, t * n (README.md).
no_counts: B24 does not apply: the counter, t * n, shows every add happened
notes: Written by std-sync2 for review finding SYNC2-R6 (status/std-sync2.md, M6 fix round): the AtomicInt rows of the audit table had no bench. Every column is the same lock-prefixed RMW on one contended cache line; Mk's Add adds the overflow check and returns the new value, so it is a lock xadd where a column whose result is unused may compile to lock add.
